Revised assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR): The FOMC statement points to a still-solid macro backdrop—strong labor markets, robust household spending, and inflation near the symmetric 2% goal—alongside a gradualist policy path and continued use of floor-system tools (IOER and ON RRP) to keep the effective funds rate within the 2.25–2.50% target range. However, the FSR tempers this optimism by noting that while core financial intermediaries remain resilient and near-term funding risks are low, key vulnerabilities persist: asset valuations in some markets are elevated, corporate leverage—especially among lower-rated firms—is high, and risk sentiment has become more fragile amid global and market volatility. These stability considerations nudge risks from “roughly balanced” toward slightly more two-sided than the statement alone suggests, reinforcing a more guarded, data-dependent stance. Net tone: constructive but more cautious than before.
